correctness.rationale: A leaf-edge congruence splits off a nonsingular 2-by-2 alternating block and leaves the weighted forest with the leaf and its neighbour removed. The matching number obeys the identical recurrence because a maximum matching can always be chosen to contain a leaf edge. Thus rank equals twice support matching number over any field. Grouping edge assignments by support gives the coefficient formula. O'Brien--Voll Theorem B gives the factor q^(n-2i), since the graphical-group abelianization has size q^n. The rooted two-state recurrence follows from whether a child can supply a new matching edge at the root. The packaged checker independently verifies all finite steps on several tree shapes and fields.

originality.rationale: Rossmann explicitly poses the character-enumeration question and records only edgeless graphs, paths, and complete graphs as solved polynomial families. The accepted theorem covers every tree and gives an explicit matching-support recurrence. O'Brien--Voll supply only the general rank-to-character conversion, while skew-rank papers study fixed oriented matrices rather than finite-field support distributions of graphical groups. Targeted database and web searches found no all-tree character formula.
residual_risks: An equivalent all-tree rank-support formula may appear in older matrix literature without graphical-group terminology.
The character result is restricted to odd q by the representation-theoretic theorem used.
The weighted-forest rank lemma is elementary; the value of the finding lies in converting it into a complete all-tree character enumeration with an explicit recurrence.

value.rationale: The result answers an explicit character-enumeration question on a broad natural graph family, extending the previously singled-out path case to every tree. It gives both a structural explanation and a computable recurrence, not merely isolated examples. The matching-support polynomial exposes exactly why trees are tractable and where cyclic graphs become harder through Pfaffian cancellation.
